# Lex Machina v2.0 — Agent Instructions (`llms.txt`)

> World's first bitemporal, SHA-256-provenanced Git corpus + deterministic anti-hallucination MCP engine for global AI, Cyber & International Law (`a-vip/lex-machina`).

## Why This Engine Eliminates Legal AI Hallucinations
1. Full-text primary ingestion from EUR-Lex CELLAR (Akoma Ntoso XHTML), Consilium/UN/CoE/NIST PDFs, and ICRC IHL with SHA-256 digests and honest `provenance_mode` tagging.
2. Concordance-aware `diff_provisions` and phrase-level institutional `blame_provision` across renumbered drafts (e.g., EU AI Act Proposal Art. 52 -> Final Art. 50; GDPR Proposal Art. 20 -> Final Art. 22).
3. Bitemporal `check_applicability` encoding 2025-2026 amendments: EU Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Annex III -> Dec 2, 2027; Annex I -> Aug 2, 2028; Art. 5 NCII/CSAM & legacy Art. 50(2) -> Dec 2, 2026), US EO 14110 revocation (Jan 20, 2025), Texas TRAIGA (Jan 1, 2026), EU CRA Art. 14 ENISA reporting (Sept 11, 2026), China Sept 1, 2025 Labeling Measures (GB 45438-2025), and UN Hanoi Cybercrime 40-ratification threshold.
4. Deterministic `verify_citations` gate enforcing ABA Formal Opinion 512 before returning any legal opinion.
5. Cross-dialect BM25 search normalizing UK <-> US legal spellings (`categorisation` <-> `categorization`, `defence` <-> `defense`) and expanding acronyms (`FRIA`, `RBI`, `GPAI`, `LAWS`, `CRA`, `DORA`, `NIS2`).

## Mandatory Agent Workflow
1. Always call `get_provision` to inspect verbatim text; if `PROVISION NOT IN CORPUS` is returned, NEVER guess from model weights.
2. Always call `check_applicability` before stating any provision is legally enforceable on a given date.
3. Always call `verify_citations` on draft memos before delivering them to the user.
4. Companion skills & Claude Code plugin: `https://github.com/a-vip/lex-machina-skills`.
